sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Kumara H V who met with road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
That on 15-07-2024 at about 3.00 p.m., Kumara H.V was traveling in a Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-MQ-2629 as an occupant and when the said vehicle reached near Channasandra RNSIT bridge Nice road, Kengeri, Bengaluru, driver driven the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the road divider, result of which vehicle jumped over the road divider and dashed against Mahindra XUV vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MZ-1122 coming from opposite lane, result of which Kumara H V sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.

So far, the petitioners have spent more than Rs.3,00,000/-
towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies.
3. Prior to the accident, Kumara was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 41 years.
He was working as a Chief executive at Hanumanahalli Dairy and also working as Agriculturist and dairy farming in Hanumanahalli and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of Kumar H V , petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the R.C. owner of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed exparte.

5. Respondent no.2 -the Insurer of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license.

6. Respondent no.3 - the Owner of Mahindra XUV vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MZ-1122 has filed written statement and contended that he is the owner of Mahindra XUV vehicle and same was insured with the respondent no.4 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

He admitted that accident was due to the rash and negligent driving of the Scorpio Car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 and that due to the accident, his vehicle was heavily damaged and unfit for repair and inmates of the Car were also suffered grievous injuries and that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Mahindra XUV vehicle.

7. The respondent no.4/ the insurer of Mahindra XUV vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MZ-1122 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.4 has contended that as per complaint, FIR, statement of witnesses, Charge sheet and other police documents the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the Scorpio vehicle bearing Mamatha T S vs Raju on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174980700/
3 Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of their insured vehicle.
8.
On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, Kumara H V, died on account of road traffic accident on 15-07-2024 at 03-00 pm., near Channasandra RNSIT bridge nice road,
Kengeri, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- MQ-2629?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
9. The petitioner No.1 got examined herself as Pw1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 and Ex.P8.

On the other hand, the respondent no.4 has examined its Senior Manager as RW.1 and got marked copy of Insurance policy at Ex.R1.
10.
Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 to 4.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

11. My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per final Order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS 12. Issue No.1: Petitioners have categorically contended that on 15-07-2024 at about 3.00 p.m.,
Kumara H V (herein after called the deceased) was traveling in a Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ- 2629 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) as an occupant and when the said vehicle reached near Channasandra RNSIT bridge Nice road, Kengeri, Bengaluru, driver of said vehicle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the road divider, result of which vehicle jumped over the road divider and dashed against Mahindra XUV vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-MZ-1122 coming from opposite lane, due to which deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Mamatha T S vs Raju on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174980700/
4 13.

In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 8 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.7 i.e., F.I.R with complaint, Spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, Inquest Mahazar, Post Mortem report and Charge sheet are the material documents to prove the present point.

14. On the basis of the complaint lodged by K.T Ankaraju, case has been registered against the driver of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 in Crime No.0121/2024 of Kengeri Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(a), 106 of BNS, 2023.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-MQ-2629 for the offences punishable under Section 281,
125(a), 106, 125 (b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, (BNS) 2023.
15.

It is not in dispute that respondent no.1 is the RC owner of the offending vehicle, respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the said vehicle, respondent no.3 is the RC owner of the Mahindra XUV Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01/MZ-1122 and respondent no.4 is the insurer of the said vehicle.
If the averments of the petition, the evidence of PW.1 and police records are perused, the deceased was the inmate in the offending vehicle.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that the deceased who was traveling in the offending vehicle was met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of said vehicle.
The respondent no.1 and 2 have not seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the offending vehicle was proceeding from Sompur Nice office road towards Hosakerehalli toll.
There is a divider between the two roads.
Mahindra XUV Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01/MZ-1122 was proceeding from Hosakerehalli toll towards Sompura Nice office road.
The offending vehicle by hitting the divider jumped to the other side of the road and hit against Mahindra XUV Car.

From the very scene of occurrence and the fact of the offending vehicle by crossing the road divider stepped into the other road and hit to the vehicle coming from opposite lane itself would reveals the speed at which the offending vehicle was at the time of accident.

Hence, without discussing much on this point it can be said without any hesitation that, the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident and for the no fault of the driver of Mahindra XUV Car, he and the inmates of the said Car have also sustained injuries.
Hence, Issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it can be said that deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 41 years.
In this regard, the petitioners have produced Ex.P8/Aadhaar card of the deceased wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 11-06-1983.

Hence it can be gathered that as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 41 years.
17.

So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was working as Chief Executive in Hanumanahalli dairy and also working as agriculturist and dairy farmer and thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.

Since accident in question has occurred in the year 2024, the court has to Mamatha T S vs Raju on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174980700/
5 consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
18.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner no.2 and 3 being the minor children and petitioner no.4 being the mother of the deceased are considered as the dependents of the deceased.

19. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife, children, mother and and they are stated to have resided together with the deceased, 1/4 th of the annual income is to be deducted towards personal expenses and remaining 3/4th is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.

20. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd) it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40% of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case, as deceased was aged around 41 years, 25% should be added towards future prospects.

21. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.16,500/-, by adding 25% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.20,625/-, out of it if th is deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.15,469/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 41 to 45 is '14'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.25,98,792/-
(Rs.15,469/- x 14 x 12 =Rs.25,98,792/- ).
22.
Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost her husband, petitioner No.2 and 3 lost their father and petitioner no.4 lost her beloved son in her old age.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

23. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Mamatha T S vs Raju on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174980700/
6

entities.text: Pranay Mamatha T S vs Raju on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.

24. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
Under the Heads 1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150-00 2 Transportation and funeral Rs.
18,150-00 expenses 3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs. 1,93,600-00 parental consortium and filial consortium (Rs.48,400x4) 4 Loss of dependency Rs.
25,98,792-00 Total Rs. 28,28,692-00
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for Rs.28,28,692/-. and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
25. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
But if the charge sheet is perused, the driver of the offending vehicle was charge sheeted even for the offence U/Sec.185 of IMV Act for his driving the vehicle under intoxication mind.

It is argued by the learned counsel for petitioners that there is no evidence to say the quantity of liquor consumed by the driver of offending vehicle so as to say that, he has violated the rules by driving the vehicle under intoxication.
But, if the charge sheet is perused, wherein it is clearly stated that the quantity of alcohol consumed by the driver was 30.643 mg., against 100 ml., of blood.
The drink and drive alcohol limit is a blood alcohol concentration of 0.03% or 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood.
Driving with a blood alcohol concentration exceeding this limit is illegal and it attracts imprisonment U/sec.185 of the Motor vehicles Act 1988.

In the present case the blood alcohol concentration in the body of the driver of the offending vehicle was 30.643 m.g., which is exceeding the limit, hence only the investigating officer filed charge sheet against the driver even for the offence punishable U/sec.185 of IMV Act.
26.

So far as the liability of paying compensation is concerned, it is true that all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of accident but, as observed supra, the driver under the drunken state of mind drive the vehicle and caused for the accident.

27. The learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 6922/2014 (MV-D) decided on 19-06-2025 between Jyothimani Mary Regina and another V/s The Manager, ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. ltd., and another.

entities.text: Jyothimani Mary Regina and another V/s The Manager, ICICI Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case also all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force, but at the time of accident the driver of the offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol.

The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has observed that the driving of vehicle under the influence of alcohol may be violation of an implied contract between insurer and insured, but as far as third party is concerned the insurer cannot dis own its liability to pay the compensation. Sec.147 and 149 of M.V. Act do not state that on that ground insurer can deny its liability to pay the compensation.

Therefore, under Mamatha T S vs Raju on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174980700/
7 such circumstances the insurer is liable to pay the compensation and it is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle, since the owner has handed over the vehicle to a person who was driving the vehicle under the influence of alcohol, contrary to provision of Sec.185 of M.V. Act.
28.

7

sentences.text: In MFA.No.4090 of 2016 (MV-I) decided on 3- 7-2025 between The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Sri.Pratik Kumar Tripathy and others.

entities.text: Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Sri.Pratik Kumar Tripathy and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the similar set of facts has ordered for pay and recovery.
In the said case the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has referred many number of judgments of different High courts decided recently, wherein also pay and recovery was ordered.

Among them the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala in the case of Mohammed Rashid @ Rashid V/s Girivasan E.K. (MACA NO.616/2018 decided on 30-01-2023 reported in 2023 live law (Kerala) 52 held that, in case of drink and drive the owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation and the insurer shall pay the compensation to the third party and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

entities.text: Mohammed Rashid @ Rashid V/s Girivasan E.K. (MACA NO.616/2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
29. In view of the observation made by the Hon'ble High courts of different States including our Hon'ble High court and also considering the fact that at the time of accident the driver was under the influence of alcohol, by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 to pay the compensation, at the first instance with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount liberty is given to recover the same from the respondent no.1.
30.
As observed supra charge sheet is filed against the offending vehicle i.e., the Scorpio Ccar in which the deceased was the inmate.

Even this court has also come to the conclusion that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident, in which the driver of the Mahindra XUV Car had played no role.
The learned counsel for petitioners at this juncture has referred judgment reported in 2022 ACJ 422 between Chauhan Vikramsinh Nansinh and another V/s Zala Arjunsinh Fatesinh and others.,

entities.text: Chauhan Vikramsinh Nansinh and another V/s Zala Arjunsinh Fatesinh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case it was found that the accident was occurred due to composite negligency of the drivers of both the vehicles and attributed negligency in the ratio of 70:30 for Truck driver and Jeep driver respectively and directed the Insurance company of Truck and the owner of Jeep to satisfy the award in the same ratio.

The question was raised before the Hon'ble High Court whether the Tribunal erred in bifurcating the amount awarded and claimants are entitled to claim entire compensation from both or any one of the joint tort feasors.

By answering the above question in the Affirmative it was ordered to pay the entire compensation by the Insurance company of Truck and directed to recover the amount from the owner of the Jeep to the extent of his liability.
31. In 2015 ACJ 1441 between Khenyei V/s New India Assurance Co. Ltd., and others., In the said case there was collusion between a Bus and Truck due to composite negligence of both the drivers.

entities.text: 2015 ACJ 1441 between Khenyei V/s New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respective blame for the Truck driver being 2/3rd and that of Bus driver was 1/3rd.
The question was raised whether the claimants are entitled to claim entire compensation from both or any one of the joint tort feasor.
It was held liability of joint tort feasors is joint and several.

32. The observation made in the aforesaid ruling has no application to the case in hand for the reason that the aforesaid observation is applicable only in case where there is composite negligence on the part of both the vehicles, but in the present case it is clearly proved that the accident in Mamatha T S vs Raju on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174980700/
8 question was due to the driver of the offending vehicle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Thereafter the respondent no.2 is at liberty to recover the same from respondent no.1.
Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
33. Issue No.3:-
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this point is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,28,692/-. (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Twenty Eight Thousand Six Hundred Ninety Two only) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award and to recover the said amount from the respondent no.1/owner of the offending vehicle.

Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.15,28,692/- Petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.4,00,000/- each, Petitioner No 4 is entitled for Rs.5,00,000/-
Out of the amount and interest

, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 4 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.

The entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 and 3 till they attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner no.1 to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.75,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Kumara H V who met with road traffic accident.
The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid driving license.
opennyai_summary.issue:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that, Kumara H V, died on account of road traffic accident on 15-07-2024 at 03-00 pm., near Channasandra RNSIT bridge nice road,
Kengeri, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Scorpio vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- MQ-2629?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is not in dispute that respondent no.1 is the RC owner of the offending vehicle, respondent no.2 is the Insurer of the said vehicle, respondent no.3 is the RC owner of the Mahindra XUV Vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01/MZ-1122 and respondent no.4 is the insurer of the said vehicle.
If the averments of the petition, the evidence of PW.1 and police records are perused, the deceased was the inmate in the offending vehicle.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that the deceased who was traveling in the offending vehicle was met with an accident due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of said vehicle.
The respondent no.1 and 2 have not seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners.
There is a divider between the two roads.
The offending vehicle by hitting the divider jumped to the other side of the road and hit against Mahindra XUV Car.
From the very scene of occurrence and the fact of the offending vehicle by crossing the road divider stepped into the other road and hit to the vehicle coming from opposite lane itself would reveals the speed at which the offending vehicle was at the time of accident.
Hence, without discussing much on this point it can be said without any hesitation that, the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident and for the no fault of the driver of Mahindra XUV Car, he and the inmates of the said Car have also sustained injuries.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
But if the charge sheet is perused, the driver of the offending vehicle was charge sheeted even for the offence U/Sec.185 of IMV Act for his driving the vehicle under intoxication mind.
The drink and drive alcohol limit is a blood alcohol concentration of 0.03% or 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood.
Driving with a blood alcohol concentration exceeding this limit is illegal and it attracts imprisonment U/sec.185 of the Motor vehicles Act 1988.
In the present case the blood alcohol concentration in the body of the driver of the offending vehicle was 30.643 m.g., which is exceeding the limit, hence only the investigating officer filed charge sheet against the driver even for the offence punishable U/sec.185 of IMV Act.
26.
So far as the liability of paying compensation is concerned, it is true that all the documents pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of accident but, as observed supra, the driver under the drunken state of mind drive the vehicle and caused for the accident.
In MFA.No.4090 of 2016 (MV-I) decided on 3- 7-2025 between The Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s Sri.Pratik Kumar Tripathy and others.
Even this court has also come to the conclusion that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident, in which the driver of the Mahindra XUV Car had played no role.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
Thereafter the respondent no.2 is at liberty to recover the same from respondent no.1.
Accordingly, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
33. Issue No.3:-
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this point is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.28,28,692/-. (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakh Twenty Eight Thousand Six Hundred Ninety Two only) along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award and to recover the said amount from the respondent no.1/owner of the offending vehicle.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.15,28,692/- Petitioner No.2 & 3 are entitled for Rs.4,00,000/- each, Petitioner No 4 is entitled for Rs.5,00,000/-
Out of the amount and interest
, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 4 shall be deposited in their name in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.
The entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of minor petitioner no.2 and 3 till they attains the age of majority reserving right to the petitioner no.1 to withdrawn the accrued interest for the maintenance and welfare of the minor.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
